welcome_lead: Time to crunch half-lives, balance decay equations, and rank ionising power.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics Radioactive Decay calculations — half-life powers of two, decay equations and conservation of A and Z.
final_note: You can now halve samples through multiple half-lives and balance alpha and beta decay equations.

concepts.def: Nuclear equation where A and Z are conserved on both sides
A drops by 4, Z drops by 2; emits ⁴₂He
A unchanged, Z rises by 1; a neutron becomes a proton
Alpha > beta > gamma — alpha rips off the most electrons
Gamma > beta > alpha — gamma travels furthest in matter

walkthroughs.body_html:
After n half-lives, the fraction remaining is (½)n.

1 half-life → ½. 2 → ¼. 3 → 1/8. 4 → 1/16.

So if you start with 1600 nuclei and 3 half-lives pass, you have 1600 × ⅛ = 200 left.

In alpha decay, the nucleus loses a helium-4 nucleus (⁴₂He).

So mass number A drops by 4 and atomic number Z drops by 2.

Example: ²³⁸₉₂U → ²³⁴₉₀Th + ⁴₂He. Check: 238 = 234 + 4 ✓ and 92 = 90 + 2 ✓.

In beta decay, a neutron turns into a proton plus an emitted electron.

So A stays the same and Z goes up by 1.

Example: ¹⁴₆C → ¹⁴₇N + ⁰₋₁e. Check: 14 = 14 + 0 ✓ and 6 = 7 + (−1) ✓.

mcqs.q: A nuclide undergoes alpha decay. What happens to its mass number A and atomic number Z?
options: A drops 4, Z drops 2
A drops 2, Z drops 4
A unchanged, Z up 1
A up 4, Z up 2

mcqs.q: Which radiation is the MOST ionising but LEAST penetrating?
options: Gamma
Beta
Alpha
X-ray

mcqs.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is most ionising?
options: Alpha radiation — large, doubly charged particles cause the most ionisation per unit distance.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
Gamma is most ionising because it can travel furthest and pass through almost anything.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.

mcqs.q: What absorber is needed to stop beta radiation?
options: A sheet of paper — beta is only slightly more penetrating than alpha.
A few millimetres of aluminium (or similar thin metal sheet).
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.

mcqs.q: After one half-life, what happens to an individual radioactive nucleus?
options: The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
Every nucleus is guaranteed to have half-decayed after one half-life.
It has a 50 percent chance of having decayed — radioactive decay is random for any single nucleus.
Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
